A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with v2 adding the GaussianVision name and substantially extending the study. Text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. v1 ends with references; v2 includes an accessible appendix in Sections 8–11.

before.justification: v1 reports original CUDA speed measurements, initialization and pruning experiments, and zero-shot ImageNet results for its Gaussian-splat encoders.

after.justification: v2 reports original cross-dataset classification results, profiling measurements, pruning studies, and extensive architecture and training ablations, including appendix results.

M1.justification: v1 directly adapts an RGB-initialized GS encoder through CLIP training. v2 introduces a preceding vision-only distillation stage matching normalized RGB and GS CLS embeddings, followed by CLIP adaptation with optional text-side unfreezing (Section 5.2). Its stem also changes from the gated, z-score/global-mean design in v1 Figure 5 to the simpler normalization and projection path in v2 Figure 1d and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Training retains the 12.8M DataComp dataset, but evaluation expands far beyond ImageNet-1K to fine-grained recognition, medical and satellite imagery, rendered-text sentiment, synthetic spatial tasks, and shifted ImageNet/ObjectNet inputs. v2 describes 38 datasets, although Table 5 contains 37 dataset rows; the substantial coverage expansion is clear despite that discrepancy.

E2.justification: v2 adds 98-token RGB comparisons without fine-tuning and with one or five fine-tuning epochs (Table 7), plus rendered-RGB, grid/convolutional-stem, and point-transformer comparisons (Figures 18–20). The ViT-L/16 comparator plotted in v1 Figure 7 is absent from the corresponding v2 studies. These change the evaluated comparator set, beyond extending existing models to more datasets.

E3.justification: The reported GS training budget changes from six adaptation epochs to two distillation epochs followed by five CLIP epochs. v2 adds explicit RGB token-merging/fine-tuning controls, cross-dataset absolute and dataset-wise relative accuracy summaries, load/decode timing on batches of 256, and pruning sweeps over 100 images per configuration. These are substantive protocol additions, while the main RGB training recipe remains largely retained.

E4.justification: v1 mainly examines initialization, qualitative pruning, splat/token budgets, and training from scratch. v2 adds quantitative pruning sensitivity and convergence analyses, plus controlled studies of distillation order and losses, normalization, learning rates, text freezing, alternative stems, point transformers, reconstructed RGB inputs, and direct Gaussian tokenization (Sections 9 and 11.5–11.6). These test substantially more explanations for performance and optimization behavior.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 4 newly uses KDE summaries to estimate empirical distributions of pruning and PSNR outcomes across configurations. This adds descriptive statistical estimation, rather than repeated-training uncertainty. Neither version reports seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its classification results.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive dataset-level scores, timing results, and ablation findings. For example, Table 5 reports 16.87% ImageNet top-1 for GS-1600 with 196 tokens under the revised training procedure; this is not a same-protocol gain over v1's reported 13–15% range. The earlier top-5 summary is absent. Initialization PSNR examples also change alongside the illustrated image, whereas Figure 2 retains the original 90.3× fitting-speed result.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.4 newly specifies the exact batch-averaged reconstruction-plus-L1 objective, weighted absolute-RGB luminance score, and retained-splat index set, which v1 leaves verbally specified. This is a limited addition of mathematical definitions. The Gaussian reconstruction equation is unchanged, and neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims preliminary viability despite an ImageNet accuracy gap. v2 presents two-stage alignment as a central contribution and claims competitive performance across a broad benchmark, retaining 90–98% mean dataset-wise relative RGB accuracy while providing substantial loading-speed benefits. This materially broadens the central effectiveness and efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about offline fitting cost, dependence on the RGB teacher, sensitivity to distribution shifts, and alignment using non-pruned FP16 splats. Its appendix interprets reconstructed-RGB experiments as evidence about compression-limited performance and architectural studies as evidence for a token bottleneck. These extend v1's discussion of the accuracy gap, weak scratch training, and omitted quantization.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents preprocessing iterations and batch sizes, estimated fitting GPU-hours, normalization statistics, Fourier frequencies, Perceiver dimensions and heads, and forward-pass pseudocode (Tables 3–4 and Section 11.2). These substantially improve implementation specificity without establishing that every newly disclosed setting changed. Code release remains prospective, with v2 expanding the promised release to the full preprocessing and CLIP pipeline.

R1.justification: The main positioning against pixel-based tokenization, INRs, GaussianImage, and earlier Gaussian recognition methods is retained. v2 adds references and discussion for CLIP Benchmark, VTAB, and contrastive representation distillation, principally supporting its expanded evaluation and loss studies rather than redefining its relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the presentation: it adds the GaussianVision name, condenses preliminaries, moves CLIP background from Section 3.3 to appendix Section 8.1, rewrites the alignment section around setup/training/protocol/results, and separates Discussion from Conclusion. The structured appendix further reorganizes technical explanations and analyses; this exceeds a simple content extension or renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 redraws and combines the overview and GS architecture into a first-page Figure 1, replaces the qualitative pruning display with quantitative plots and new examples, and replaces the ImageNet-only result display with a broad benchmark chart. It adds substantial comparative tables, profiling displays, and ablation panels throughout the appendix. These are extensive visual and layout changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow validation and limited support for its design choices through broader evaluation, token-matched RGB controls, and targeted distillation and architecture ablations. Detailed preprocessing and model specifications also improve reproducibility. Reporting defects remain: 38 datasets are claimed but 37 are tabulated, and Table 3's speedup column matches batch-time ratios rather than throughput speedups. These weaken particular summaries but do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and technical transparency.
